info.name: Book content type — Open Library (design spike)
info.description:
Exercises the three Open Library endpoints the Book content type design (`docs/superpowers/specs/2026-11-09-book-content-type-discover-design.md`) relies on, before any backend adapter exists. Nothing here hits the Perspectize backend — there is no `BookSearchClient`/`BookTrendingClient`/`BookISBNClient` yet. This collection is the reference for building those adapters: every URL and `fields=` list here is what the design doc assumes.

### Adapter facts encoded here
- Base URL `https://openlibrary.org`
- No API key, no auth, no quota — confirmed live 2026-11-09
- `search.json` and `trending/{window}.json` return the *same* work-shaped item and both honor `fields=`; `isbn/{isbn}.json` is a different shape (a 302 to a specific **edition**, which Postman follows automatically)
- The `fields=` list used throughout (`key,title,author_name,cover_i,first_publish_year,number_of_pages_median,subject,ratings_average,ratings_count,edition_count`) is exactly what `CreateFromBook` needs in one call (design doc §4)
- Folder 2 proves the design doc's §7a/§7b findings live: an edition's own `number_of_pages` differs from the work's `number_of_pages_median`; `genres` is often empty and needs a second lookup

### Setup
No variables need changing to run this as-is. `work_key`/`isbn` point at *East of Eden* throughout — swap them to explore a different book. Run folders in order; Folder 2's requests depend on values Folder 0/1 return (noted per-request).

variable.description: Exactly what the design doc's CreateFromBook/BookSearchResult needs (§4). Trimmed from a search/trending response — see Folder 0's test scripts.
daily | weekly — the two the design doc reuses from domain.TrendingWindow (§3). monthly/yearly/now/forever exist on Open Library but are deferred.
East of Eden's work id. Auto-filled from Folder 0a's top result by its test script.
ISBN-13 for the 1970 Heinemann East of Eden reprint (OL22640535M) — resolves to the same work_key above, the dedupe case design doc §2 describes.

A well-formed, unassigned ISBN-13 confirmed live 2026-11-09 to 404. Caution: not every nonsense-looking ISBN 404s — "9999999999999" surprisingly resolved to an unrelated real record (a 2026-11-09 finding), so client-side checksum validation matters more than assuming Open Library will reject garbage.
A real sparse record (no cover, no rating) — design doc §7a/§7b's edge case.

item.name: 0. Quickstart — Search and Trending
item.description: The two Discover-tab data sources (design doc §1). Both return a work-shaped item list and both honor `fields=`.

exec: pm.test('has at least one doc', () => body.docs && body.docs.length > 0);

request.description: Design doc §1: confirmed live 2026-11-09 that the top result for "East of Eden Steinbeck" is the work itself (/works/OL23166W), not a random edition, with author_name, cover_i, first_publish_year=1952, number_of_pages_median=611, subject[] (65 entries), ratings_average=4.1, ratings_count=100.

Design doc §1/§6: the response shape matches 0a exactly (same `fields=` support), but the content skews toward current nonfiction bestsellers (Atomic Habits, The 48 Laws of Power as of 2026-11-09) rather than classics — the UI disclosure this finding drove.

item.name: 1. ISBN tab — resolve a specific edition
item.description: Design doc §5: the ISBN tab's resolution path. isbn/{isbn}.json 302s to an edition record; the edition's works[0].key feeds back into the same search.json lookup as Folder 0a to get the full BookSearchResult shape.

exec: pm.test('has a works[] back-reference', () => body.works && body.works.length > 0);

console.log('Edition', body.key, 'number_of_pages:', body.number_of_pages, '— compare to the work-level number_of_pages_median from 0a (611). Different numbers: one is a single printing, the other a cross-edition median (design doc §7a).');

request.description: Confirmed live 2026-11-09: GET /isbn/9780434740024.json → 302 → /books/OL22640535M.json, the 1970 Heinemann East of Eden edition. Its own number_of_pages (525) differs from the work's search-index number_of_pages_median (611) — the exact distinction design doc §7a documents. Note: the edition record has no author_name/ratings_average/number_of_pages_median of its own — only Folder 0a-style search gives those.

item.name: 1b - works/{work_key}.json (canonical record — description, genres, subject split)

request.description: Design doc §4/§7b: this canonical record has `description` (not fetched in v1 — needs this separate call) and a `genres` field — but `genres` is an array of opaque /tags/{id} references, often empty, and resolving each one to a label needs yet another call. This is the evidence behind "no genre/theme split, reuse the shared Tags column" (§7b). Also lacks author_name, ratings_average, and number_of_pages_median — those are search-index aggregates (Folder 0), not on this record.

item.name: 2. Edge cases
item.description: The states the design doc's testing section (and the preview's sparse/not-found rows) must cover.

request.description: Design doc §5's error case: "No book found for that ISBN" — the ISBN tab must surface this cleanly, not as a raw 404/500.
Confirmed live 2026-11-09: Brainscan (a zine) has no cover_i and no ratings_average/ratings_count at all — the "unknown, not zero" row the preview's sparse-fill example is built from.
